title: AI-Augmented Fraud Detection in Cloud Platforms: GRA-Based Risk Ranking with Cybersecurity and Threat Prevention for SAP HANA Healthcare ERP
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Computer Science & Technology (IJARCST)
tldr: Proposes a DevOps-centric AI fraud detection framework combining graph-based risk ranking with supervised and unsupervised models for SAP HANA healthcare ERP, using synthetic data evaluation.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional fraud detection systems rely on rule-based engines or batch classifiers that struggle with zero-day attacks, multi-entity fraud rings, and high false positives. They lack integration with modern DevOps workflows for rapid model iteration.
approach: Designed a pipeline integrating data ingestion, preprocessing, feature extraction, graph construction, and model scoring stages.
Implemented a Graph-Risk-Adaptive (GRA) ranking module using entity graphs to compute risk-based rankings.
Combined supervised classification with unsupervised anomaly detection and graph-based relational risk scoring.
Built CI/CD pipeline using Azure DevOps and GitHub for automated orchestration of data and model lifecycle.
Evaluated on synthetic transactional data simulating petabyte-scale cloud-native environments with fraud rings and concept drift.
findings: num: Hybrid supervised+GRA model consistently outperformed supervised-only and supervised+anomaly baselines.
Graph-based risk ranking captures complex fraud patterns (fraud rings, synthetic identities) missed by classifiers alone.
DevOps integration enables rapid model updates and continuous adaptation to new fraud patterns.
Combining classification with graph scoring reduces false positives by filtering out benign anomalies.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces a graph-based risk ranking approach to fraud detection that captures relational fraud patterns missed by traditional classifiers. It demonstrates the value of DevOps-centric pipeline orchestration for continuous model adaptation in production environments. The hybrid architecture combining supervised and graph-based methods offers a framework for reducing false positive rates while maintaining detection coverage.
directly_justifies: Graph-based risk ranking detects fraud rings and synthetic identity fraud.
DevOps CI/CD integration enables rapid adaptation to evolving fraud patterns.
limits: Evaluation on synthetic data may not fully capture real-world complexity and noise.
Healthcare ERP focus may not generalize to personal finance transaction monitoring.
Graph construction overhead at petabyte scale may become a performance bottleneck.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) was flagged as high relevance because the paper's core contribution is fraud detection methodology. Domain 14.B (ML Serving) was flagged as high because DevOps pipeline integration is a central contribution. All other domains (1-7, 9-13) were rejected as the paper addresses cloud infrastructure fraud detection, not personal finance.

limitations: Synthetic data evaluation may not generalize to real-world production environments.
Graph construction and computation overhead at petabyte scale not fully addressed.
Operational complexity of the full pipeline requires specialized engineering teams.
